stories.headline: SK Hynix in talks with Intel to make memory chips in the US for the first time

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix is in talks with Intel about a deal that would have it manufacture memory chips on US soil for the first time, three people familiar with the discussions said on September 16.
key_facts.excerpt: SEOUL/WASHINGTON, Sept 16 (Reuters) - South Korea's SK Hynix is in talks with Intel about a deal that would see it manufacture memory chips on U.S. soil for the first time, three people familiar with the discussions said.

key_facts.fact: Under one scenario SK Hynix would lease part of Intel's long-planned Ohio chipmaking facility; under another it would form a venture with Intel and major cloud firms seeking to lock in memory supply.
key_facts.excerpt: Under one potential scenario, SK Hynix would lease part of Intel's long-planned chipmaking facility in Ohio, they said. Under another scenario, it could form a venture with Intel and major cloud firms that are keen to lock in memory chip supplies, two of the people said.

key_facts.fact: Intel announced in 2022 it would invest up to $100 billion in the Ohio complex with production due in 2025; the two plants have slipped to 2030 and 2031.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel announced in 2022 that it would invest up to $100 billion to build potentially the world's largest chipmaking complex in Ohio, with production scheduled to begin in 2025. But completion of the site's two plants has since been delayed to 2030 and 2031.

key_facts.fact: Seoul is a potential obstacle: producing advanced memory such as HBM or DRAM abroad could be treated as a 'national core technology' subject to review under South Korea's Industrial Technology Protection Act.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked about a potential SK Hynix plan to produce chips in the U.S., South Korea's trade ministry said any decision would be at the company's discretion but if it involved a "national core technology," it would be subject to a review under the Industrial Technology Protection Act.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix publicly pushed back the same day, saying no decisions had been made on either scenario described in the report.
key_facts.excerpt: "No decisions have been made regarding the two scenarios mentioned in the article," SK hynix said. "Nothing has been finalized regarding cooperation with any specific companies mentioned in the article or memory chip production in the US."

key_facts.fact: Shares of both Intel and SK Hynix rose in premarket trading on the report; a deal would be a marquee foundry win for CEO Lip-Bu Tan's strategy.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix is in talks with Intel to manufacture its memory chips in the U.S. for the first time, Reuters reported Wednesday, sending shares of both companies higher in premarket trading.

stories.headline: Anthropic signs first Australian data center lease: a 2.16GW, A$32bn campus in Queensland

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed its first Australian data center lease on September 16, covering a planned campus with 2.16 gigawatts of capacity about 250 km from Brisbane, due to start coming online in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The lease covers a data centre campus with planned capacity totalling 2.16 gigawatts, one of the people said, on par with some of the largest centres currently operating worldwide. The proposed facility on farmland about 250 km (150 miles) from Brisbane is planned to start coming online in 2027.

key_facts.fact: Queensland Premier David Crisafulli announced the deal in state Parliament, calling it 'an historic agreement for their first Australian data centre'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Earlier today, Anthropic signed an historic agreement for their first Australian data centre," he said in Queensland's Parliament on Sept 16.

key_facts.fact: The site is the Western Downs Digital Park near Dalby, built by Singapore-owned Zerra DC, with an expected build cost of about A$32 billion — nearly five times the Brisbane 2032 Olympics infrastructure budget.
key_facts.excerpt: AI company Anthropic has signed an agreement to use part of a $32 billion data centre proposed for a site on Queensland's Western Downs... The multi-billion-dollar investment in is almost five times greater than the 2032 Brisbane Olympic and Paralympic Games infrastructure budget.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic will take the entire capacity of the park on a long-term lease and use it for inference — serving Claude customer requests — rather than training, and will go to market for a renewable power purchase agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic, led by chief executive Dario Amodei, will take the entire capacity of the Western Downs Digital Park, near Dalby, through a long-term lease of the Singapore-owned Zerra DC's proposed AI factory. The company will then go to market to secure a long-term power purchase agreement.

key_facts.fact: The deal still needs Foreign Investment Review Board approval and local council sign-off; the development application was only filed with the council last month.
key_facts.excerpt: Deal is subject to Foreign Investment Review Board approval

key_facts.fact: The campus is planned as four buildings of 36,000 square metres each, air-cooled to avoid straining local water resources; its power draw is comparable to 1.5 million average Australian households.
key_facts.excerpt: Plans for the Western Downs Digital Park, where Anthropic will lease a data centre, show four buildings, each with 36,000 sq m of data centre floor space... The data centre will create jobs, add electricity to the grid, and use air-cooled technology to avoid straining local water resources.

stories.headline: Apple plans a return to servers: an AI box with two or four M8 Ultras, possibly using Nvidia NVLink

key_facts.fact: Apple has discussed using Nvidia's NVLink Fusion networking technology in a planned AI inference server powered by its own chips, The Information reported on September 16.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has discussed using Nvidia's NVLink Fusion networking technology in a planned AI inference server powered by its own chips, marking a potential return to the server market, the Information reported on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The machine is aimed at AI developers, businesses and governments, and could come in versions with either two or four of Apple's planned M8 Ultra chips, its highest-performance processors.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple is developing an enterprise AI server for AI developers, businesses and governments that could come in versions featuring either two or four planned M8 Ultra chips, its highest-performance processors, the Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The product is not expected before 2029 and could still be cancelled or launched without Nvidia technology.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has considered using NVLink Fusion to connect M8 chips in its planned AI server, which is not expected before 2029 and could still be canceled or launched without Nvidia technology, according to The Information.

key_facts.fact: Apple last sold dedicated server hardware under the Xserve line, discontinued in 2011.
key_facts.excerpt: The iPhone maker last sold dedicated server hardware under its Xserve line, which was discontinued in 2011 after shifting its enterprise focus to standard Mac hardware and consumer devices.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia recently opened NVLink Fusion for licensing by third parties, letting outside chips and accelerators plug into its data center infrastructure; relations between Apple and Nvidia have been strained for nearly two decades.
key_facts.excerpt: Relations between the two tech giants have been strained for nearly two decades, following an alleged defect in Nvidia graphics chips that caused widespread MacBook failures and led Apple to sever ties.

stories.headline: Rune raises $40M to put AI data centers inside solar farms, bypassing the grid entirely

key_facts.fact: Rune unveiled RELIC (Renewable Energy Linked Intelligent Compute), a modular compute system installed directly at solar generation sites, alongside a $40 million Series A led by Spark Capital.
key_facts.excerpt: Rune today unveiled RELIC (Renewable Energy Linked Intelligent Compute), a modular compute system that installs directly at solar generation sites... Alongside the launch, Rune announced a $40 million Series A led by Spark Capital, with participation from Union Square Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, Activate Capital, Committed Capital, Timeless Partners, and Logos Fund, bringing the company's total funding to $53.5 million.

key_facts.fact: Solar plants waste up to 20% of the power they generate — an estimated 50-plus terawatt hours a year in the US — which RELIC taps at the source, skipping the meter and the grid interconnection queue.
key_facts.excerpt: Solar plants waste up to 20% of the energy they generate: power produced but never sold or delivered to the grid, an estimated 50-plus terawatt hours a year in the U.S. alone. RELIC taps that stranded electricity at the source, skipping the meter, the fees, and the grid infrastructure that has stalled AI buildout across the country.

key_facts.fact: The company says customers can be energized in as little as six weeks from contract versus years for a traditional build, and that it cuts non-compute infrastructure costs by 85% — $620 million of savings at 100MW scale.
key_facts.excerpt: Faster: Installs in ~60 minutes. Compute customers are energized in as little as six weeks from contract, versus years for traditional data center builds. Cheaper: Cuts ... by 85% compared to traditional AI data centers, $620 million in savings on a 100...

key_facts.fact: Rune disclosed a live RELIC deployment at a 200MW solar facility in Texas, running with no site modifications, no grid work and no construction.
key_facts.excerpt: Rune is also revealing its latest deployment: a RELIC installation at a 200MW solar facility in Texas, live on an existing renewable asset with no site modifications, no grid work, and no construction.

key_facts.fact: The 8-by-8-foot modules run natively on DC power — solar's native output — eliminating AC conversion and the transformers now in short supply; gas plants face up to four-year transformer delays.
key_facts.excerpt: "Solar produces direct current electricity; computers run on direct current electricity," says Layden. "Nothing connected them before Rune." ... It avoids the supply chain challenges that other approaches face, including gas power plants, which can face four-year delays for transformers... the company just places its 8-by-8-foot modules on site using a forklift.

key_facts.fact: Spark Capital's Santo Politi called Rune 'the fastest path to new capacity we have seen,' arguing every operating renewable asset becomes a potential deployment site.
key_facts.excerpt: "Demand for AI infrastructure is growing faster than it can be delivered. Rune deploys compute directly behind the meter at operating solar farms, converting clean power into rapidly scalable AI capacity," said Santo Politi, Founder and General Partner of Spark Capital. "Every renewable asset in operation becomes a potential deployment site. Rune is the fastest path to new capacity we have seen."

stories.headline: GS Group files plan for a 2.4GW AI data center in Korea, first phase 15 trillion won

key_facts.fact: Regulatory filings published September 16 show GS will build a 2.4GW data center through a new subsidiary, GS AI Infrastructure, with a first 1.2GW phase in Donghae City, Gangwon Province, targeted for completion from 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the Financial Supervisory Service's electronic disclosure system on the 16th, GS[078930] plans to build a total 2.4 gigawatt (GW) data center through its newly established subsidiary GS AI Infrastructure, dedicated to AI data center construction. The initial phase targets completion of a 1.2 gigawatt (GW) facility in Donghae City, Gangwon Province from 2028.

key_facts.fact: The first-phase investment is about 15 trillion won ($12.7 billion), with GS putting up roughly 20% (about 3 trillion won) in equity and financing the rest through project finance.
key_facts.excerpt: The first-phase investment amounts to approximately 15 trillion won ($12.7 billion). GS will inject about 20% as equity capital and cover the remainder through project financing (PF). Simple calculation puts equity investment at approximately 3 trillion won ($2.5 billion).

key_facts.fact: Direct investment across the full 2.4GW build is estimated at 30 trillion won ($25.4 billion), and could reach 120 trillion won ($101 billion) including GPU and memory costs, which tenants would supply themselves.
key_facts.excerpt: While investment in the 2.4GW data center is expected to be 30 trillion won ($25.4 billion), including graphics processing unit (GPU) and memory costs, it could reach up to 120 trillion won ($101 billion). Client companies will bring in GPU infrastructure they own or have secured into the center.

key_facts.fact: Construction is set to start in November at 100-150MW scale, with incremental additions; site acquisition, permits and power procurement are due within this year.
key_facts.excerpt: The company plans site acquisition, licensing, and power procurement within this year, followed by construction start in November at 100-150MW scale.

key_facts.fact: GS is courting global big tech tenants rather than domestic ones, as the 2.4GW plan would be the largest in Asia outside Korea; no counterparties have been disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: Given that the group's planned total data center capacity of 2.4GW is reported to be the largest in Asia beyond the domestic market, the company is focusing attention on global big tech firms rather than domestic enterprises. The group stated it is currently in discussions with multiple tenants, though specific negotiation counterparties and contract stages have not been disclosed.

key_facts.fact: GS owns an underused coal plant in Donghae — utilization was 29.6% in the second quarter — raising the prospect of powering the campus from it, though GS has not yet applied to KEPCO for supply.
key_facts.excerpt: GS Donghae Power is a coal-fired power plant operated by GS Group in the Donghae region. GS Donghae Power's utilization rate was 29.6% in the second quarter of this year... GS recently passed final review of the power system impact assessment related to the data center business and is yet to apply to Korea Electric Power Corporation for power supply.

stories.headline: Crusoe signs multi-year deal to run Perplexity's models on Nvidia GB300 NVL72 clusters

key_facts.fact: Crusoe announced a multi-year partnership with Perplexity on September 15 under which Perplexity runs its full model lifecycle on Crusoe Cloud — training on dedicated Nvidia GB300 NVL72 clusters with InfiniBand, and serving via Crusoe's Managed Inference service.
key_facts.excerpt: SAN FRANCISCO, CA – September 15, 2026 – Crusoe, the industry's first vertically integrated AI infrastructure provider, today announced a multi-year partnership with Perplexity to power its AI workloads on Crusoe Cloud. Under the agreement, Perplexity will run its full model lifecycle on a single platform: training frontier models on Crusoe's dedicated NVIDIA GB300 NVL72-powered clusters, NVIDIA InfiniBand Solutions, and serving them in production through Crusoe's Managed Inference service.

key_facts.fact: In a reciprocal leg of the deal, Crusoe will deploy Perplexity Enterprise Pro and Max to its more than 1,800 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: In addition, Crusoe will adopt Perplexity Enterprise Pro and Max for its 1,800 employees, equipping them with a leading AI platform for web and internal knowledge search, multi-step research, data analysis, and access to frontier AI models.

key_facts.fact: Crusoe will host and manage the Nvidia chips over their full lifetime, Crusoe SVP Erwan Menard said.
key_facts.excerpt: Perplexity will use Nvidia Corp. AI chips from Crusoe to train and run models, as well as relying on Crusoe to manage the technology over its lifetime, Erwan Menard, a Crusoe senior vice president who oversees the cloud product, said in an interview.

key_facts.fact: The deal lands twelve days after Crusoe's roughly $13 billion, five-year cloud contract with Jane Street, which came with a $3 billion raise valuing Crusoe at $30 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: For Crusoe, the partnership is another headline-grabbing contract in what's been a breakout stretch. Earlier in September, the company announced an approximately $13 billion five-year AI cloud contract with Jane Street, the quantitative trading firm.

key_facts.fact: Perplexity already has commitments with AWS and a reported $750 million Azure deal from January 2026; Crusoe becomes a third infrastructure partner specialized in AI workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: The company already has substantial commitments with AWS and struck a $750 million deal with Microsoft Azure reported back in January 2026. Adding Crusoe to the mix gives Perplexity a third major infrastructure partner, one that specializes in AI workloads rather than general-purpose cloud computing.
